extracted.intended_audience: biomedical researchers, NIH grant applicants, and academic scientists interested in grant review and postgraduate training issues
extracted.subtask_description: Observations about what NIAID summary statements emphasize for R21/R01 competitiveness (investigator, preliminary data, approach, innovation, collaborators) and scoring realities; useful for applicants preparing grant proposals. Also contains brief commentary on doctoral program performance expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding score threshold / scoring system
rubrics_metrics.description: First thing you notice is that it takes a perfect score to get funded. Three of the four received 10s and the fourth limped home with an 11. Remember, the study section score range starts at 1, which is then multiplied by 10 after the voting of the entire panel is averaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware of how study section scoring works (1–9 averaged then multiplied by 10) and that, in practice, funded examples shown had essentially top scores (10 or 11). This implies high competitiveness and narrow paylines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accomplished investigator and research team
rubrics_metrics.description: From the Dow summary statement’s resume of discussion: 'Strengths of the application include the accomplished investigator and research team...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer praise for a strong, accomplished PI and team is cited as a clear strength; applicants should demonstrate investigators' qualifications and collective expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong / compelling preliminary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple summary statements emphasize 'strong preliminary data' and 'compelling preliminary data' as a strength; individual critique: 'Strong and compelling preliminary data is presented that indicate a high likelihood of success.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary data are repeatedly treated as critical evidence of feasibility and probability of success — applicants should present robust, relevant pilot/precedent data to convince reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct, doable, and logical experiments (Approach/feasibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: From Dow summary: 'the direct doable and logical set of experiments' is listed as a strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers value clear, realistic, logically sequenced experimental plans. Overly speculative or poorly specified approaches weaken competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for paradigm-shifting insights (impact/importance)
rubrics_metrics.description: From Dow summary: 'the likelihood of paradigm shifting insights into meliodosis' is cited as a strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications that make a plausible case for high impact or paradigm-shifting outcomes are viewed favorably; articulate potential significance and how results could change the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation / novel strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: From the Starnbach resume: 'Strengths of the application include the innovative use of the novel GPS strategy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel methods, strategies, or conceptual advances are recognized strengths. Explain what is new and why it matters compared with existing approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator track record in the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Starnbach resume: 'an investigator with a strong bacterial pathogenesis research track record' is a strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A documented history of productive research in the proposal’s domain increases reviewer confidence; include prior achievements relevant to the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellent and appropriate set of collaborators
rubrics_metrics.description: Starnbach resume: 'an excellent and appropriate set of collaborators' is listed among strengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble collaborators whose expertise fills gaps and is clearly necessary for the project; justify roles and show prior successful collaboration if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: High degree of confidence that important results will emerge (likelihood of success)
rubrics_metrics.description: Starnbach resume: 'a high degree of confidence that important results will emerge from these studies.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should convince reviewers of the reasonable probability of achieving meaningful results — through rationale, preliminary data, and feasible methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctoral program should know graduate destinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Thought of the day: 'if the core faculty of a doctoral program cannot reel off a good thumbnail sketch of their graduate’s professional destinations, there is a problem.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should track and be able to summarize alumni career outcomes; this is an indicator of program alignment with professional training goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top doctoral programs should show steady faculty placements
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'top' program that cannot point to a healthy and steady number of faculty appointments over last decades....isn't.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term placement of graduates into faculty positions is used as an evaluative signal of program quality; programs should document and communicate placement records.
